note: The source of split-partition-implicit-case-twins-in-different-years-bind-to-one-split, whose split 1.5.kon is authored in sample.toml. Here the split is pinned only in the generated sample.auto.toml, and there is no slug_state.toml, so the scb zone is churning and the generated layer is inactive. The inactive pin still drives the implicit partition of Kon and KON onto ('accepted-partition', '1.5.kon'), but no provider key is derived for it, because the key comes from the converted naming and the churning zone converts no generated pin. The refusal names that key: the `accepted-partition` part with the pin's native id 1.5.kon, read from sample.auto.toml. The replaced test resolved a plain native variable with no provider key and expected the bare refusal; the pipeline derives a key for every native variable, so the partition key is the build's only route to it (found by #1316). The second replaced test passed a naming ambiguity beside the missing key; no build forms an ambiguous family without a provider-key entry, and the refusal is raised in `resolve_source_scope` before any ambiguity is attributed, so this case reaches the same raise without one. Until the located-errors fix the build aborted there with the bare ValueError `missing explicit provider key mapping`, even in diagnostic mode. A diagnostic build now withholds the split as it withholds any key with no provider key: one unresolved_catalog_identity error on that key, no variable built; step 2 is the strict refusal.
fails_if: `resolve_source_scope` (source_scope.py) stops treating a partition split with no provider-key entry as an unresolved catalog identity in a diagnostic build, so the build aborts again, or publishes the split's states with a null provider key

sources.description: Variable 5 delivers column Kon in 2020 (CVID 20) and KON in 2021 (CVID 21).
